text:
This looks like mid-2010. Unemployment is 9.5%, which fits June or July 2010. The 10-year yield at 3.03% and the 2-year at 0.59% suggest end of June or August 2010.

The VIX at 24 fits both the June and August 2010 readings. Equities rose 6.8% over the month, and the 3-month return is -6.7%, so this is a month after a sharp drop. That pattern fits July 2010: equities rose about 7% that month, the S&P was down from April to June, and the drawdown is about -9%.

Other cues point the same way. At the end of July 2010 the 10-year yield was about 2.9–3.0%, and the 2-year was about 0.57%. Unemployment was 9.5% in June and 9.5% in July. Gold fell 5% in June but rose in July, which conflicts with the gold cue, so I rechecked the timing. Gold in July 2010 was roughly flat to down, from about 1244 to 1182, so a drop of about 5% fits.

Core CPI at 0.97% year over year fits mid-2010. Payroll growth was boosted by census hiring. I settle on July 2010.
